audit.summary: Archived assessment: Major. A7 permits counterexample to A10 strict direction improvement; DPO support/fallback and target-dependence gap; Continual editing means inflate local gains.
limitations: P1 — A7 permits counterexample to A10 strict direction improvement — Counterevidence: Locality first-order result remains sound under its own assumptions; not an LLM benchmark counterexample

P1 — A7 permits counterexample to A10 strict direction improvement — Counterevidence and alternatives: The verbal A.7 interpretation as close directions is stronger than its actual inequality: its threshold is -11.625 here, so the almost opposite b,c satisfy the printed condition. Target detachment cannot rescue this example because the filtered target is locally constant. A conditional-softmax model is a realizability witness to the stated gradient assumptions, not a measured LLM training failure. The separate locality assumptions A.11/A.13 are not assumptions of A.10.
P2 — DPO support/fallback and target-dependence gap — Counterevidence: Finite OVERTONE loss itself is defined; interpretation may be restricted to full-support fixed targets

P2 — DPO support/fallback and target-dependence gap — Counterevidence and alternatives: Restricting support and fixing/detaching the reference for one update could define a narrower objective. A tie or abstention category could account for leftover pairwise probability, but is not specified in this proof. Finite OVERTONE loss remains well-defined in these nonconstant-logit examples; the finding is not numerical failure of that loss. Actual code detachment cannot be checked from the bounded source availability result.
P3 — Continual editing means inflate local gains — Counterevidence: Many substantial LoRA improvements remain; no blanket conclusion about raw metric validity

P3 — Continual editing means inflate local gains — Counterevidence and alternatives: The corrected named gains remain nonnegative; larger LoRA gains elsewhere are not erased. Undisclosed alternative aggregation would require explanation and would not reproduce the stated simple average from these displayed inputs. No claim that all raw component values or every other row are invalid.

P4 — Literal constant-logit filtering removes every token — Counterevidence and alternatives: Nonconstant logits with positive n retain a maximum, so this is a boundary specification defect, not evidence of a frequency or failure rate in the unavailable implementation. Changing <= to < at this boundary would also preserve tied maxima.

assumptions: Operative assumptions: epsilon=0; nonzero a,b,c,a+b; N=13 finite pretraining data. New second-token conditional probabilities (.5,.3,.2) have logit Jacobian ((-2,0),(0,0),(0,0)); preferred label 0. Old conditional is uniform with Jacobian ((-1.5,.15),(0,0),(0,0)). Use distinct first tokens after the same x to select the two contexts; first-token probabilities (.6,.3,.1) are fixed independently of theta, keeping their filter defined and their gradients zero. The old sample is one of the three old-context examples.

Operative assumptions: Three-token current law (.8,.15,.05), preferred token 2, n=.5, epsilon=0, lambda=.1. All current probabilities are strictly positive; filtering leaves only token 0. These are valid algorithm inputs. A second check uses lambda=.9 to isolate the zero-reference issue even without fallback.

Operative assumptions: Use the unweighted arithmetic mean of displayed component percentages, consistent with the named Avg. columns and neighboring rows. Original per-example values and hidden precision are unavailable.
Operative assumptions: Finite equal logits (3,3,3), n=.5. Both usual population and sample standard deviation are zero, so the result does not depend on that convention.
